title: CHECK CHARGING CIRCUIT WITHOUT LOAD / CHECK CHARGING CIRCUIT WITH LOAD

content.description: Wiring diagram showing battery, alternator, ammeter, and voltmeter connections for testing charging circuit without load. Shows wire disconnected from Terminal B.

content.text: If a battery/alternator tester is available, connect the tester to the charging circuit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
(a) If a tester is not available, connect a voltmeter and ammeter to the charging circuit as follows:

items: Disconnect the wire from terminal B of the alternator and connect it to the negative terminal of the ammeter.
Connect the test lead from the positive terminal of the ammeter to terminal B of the alternator.
Connect the positive lead of the voltmeter to terminal B of the alternator.
Connect the negative lead of the voltmeter to ground.

content.description: Two analog gauges showing ammeter and voltmeter readings

content.text: (b) Check the charging circuit as follows:
With the engine running from idling to 2,000 rpm, check the reading on the ammeter and voltmeter.

items: If the voltage reading is greater than standard voltage, replace the IC regulator.
If the voltage reading is less than standard voltage, check the IC regulator and alternator as follows: With terminal F grounded, start the engine and check the voltage reading (terminal B.
If the voltage reading is greater than standard voltage, replace the IC regulator.
If the voltage reading is less than standard voltage, check the alternator.

content.description: Illustration showing alternator with Terminal F labeled and grounding procedure

content.text: (a) With the engine running at 2,000 rpm, turn on the high beam headlights and place the heater fan control switch at HI.
(b) Check the reading on the ammeter.
If the ammeter reading is less than 30A, repair the alternator. (See page CH 5)
With the battery fully charged, sometimes the indication will be less than 30A.
